@title SolanaPda
 @notice On-chain (EVM) replica of Solana's `find_program_address` / `create_program_address`.
 @dev Solana derives a Program Derived Address by hashing the seeds, a bump byte, the program id
      and the marker `"ProgramDerivedAddress"`, then requiring the result to be OFF the ed25519
      curve (so no private key can exist for it). `find_program_address` walks the bump from 255
      downward and returns the first off-curve candidate (the "canonical" bump).
      The only non-trivial part on EVM is the off-curve test. A 32-byte value is a valid ed25519
      point iff, interpreting the low 255 bits as the little-endian `y` coordinate, the value
      `x^2 = (y^2 - 1) / (d*y^2 + 1)` is a quadratic residue in F_p (p = 2^255 - 19). We avoid a
      modular inverse by using the identity QR(u/v) == QR(u*v) for v != 0 (they differ by the
      square factor v^2), so a single Legendre symbol via the MODEXP precompile decides curve
      membership. This matches curve25519-dalek's `CompressedEdwardsY::decompress().is_some()`,
      which Solana uses for `bytes_are_curve_point`.
